name: Windows Password Spray
why: Repeated failed logons across many accounts can indicate password spraying.

name: Kerberoasting Activity
why: Unusual Kerberos service-ticket requests can expose service-account credentials.

name: Encoded PowerShell Execution
why: Encoded PowerShell commonly obscures malicious command execution.

name: AWS IAM Privilege Escalation
why: High-risk IAM changes can grant persistent or administrative cloud access.

name: CloudTrail Logging Disabled
why: Disabling audit logging can conceal malicious cloud activity.

name: S3 Public Access Change
why: Public-access changes can expose sensitive cloud data.

name: Shadow AI Service Usage
why: Unapproved generative AI access can bypass governance and data-protection controls.

name: Sensitive Data Sent to AI Service
why: Sensitive content submitted to AI services can create material data-loss risk.

name: AI Model Administration Change
why: Unexpected model, endpoint, or access-policy changes can alter AI security posture.

name: Identity MFA Failure Spike
why: Repeated MFA failures can indicate credential attacks, MFA fatigue, or attempted account takeover.

name: Unexpected Identity Privilege Grant
why: Unexpected privilege assignment can create persistent access or administrative control.

name: EDR Suspicious PowerShell Process
why: EDR process telemetry can identify encoded, hidden, or suspicious PowerShell execution chains.

name: EDR Suspicious Remote Logon
why: Remote logons from unusual sources can indicate lateral movement or compromised credentials.

name: Linux SSH Brute Force
why: Repeated SSH authentication failures can indicate brute-force or password-spraying activity.

name: Linux Privileged Shell via Sudo
why: Unexpected sudo activity that launches a privileged shell can indicate privilege escalation.

name: Suspicious DNS Resolution Activity
why: Unusual DNS patterns can indicate command-and-control, tunneling, or malicious infrastructure access.

name: Risky Inbound Firewall Activity
why: Unexpected inbound access to sensitive services can expose exploitable systems or indicate probing.

name: Network Device Configuration Change
why: Unplanned network-device configuration changes can alter routing, access controls, or monitoring visibility.

name: Threat Intelligence Observable Match
why: Known-malicious indicators provide high-value context for prioritizing suspicious hosts, domains, and addresses.

name: Enterprise Security Risk Score Spike
why: Rapid accumulation of risk against an entity can reveal multi-stage activity that individual alerts miss.

name: Anomalous Web POST Activity
why: Unusual POST volume or destinations can indicate data transfer, abuse, or compromised web activity.
